So I need a new MMO to waste my free time and money on.

Maplestory as it is right now is complete, utter, shit. So I'm not interested in playing a new game that's exactly like it. Now, a new game exactly like it was back around v0.50.. Maybe. Hell, even up to about v1.2ish, it was a pretty good game. Anything before about v0.18 is a bit too early and unrefined though.

So here's a few things I'm interested in an MMO.

  1. Social play should be rewarded in almost all situations. The best part about old Maple was how awesome all the party quests were, and how you could start doing them right at the start of the game. I loved having to communicate with people and solve simple puzzles and stuff. It was the best part of the game, in my opinion.
  2. Exploration should be rewarded. I wanna be able to find cool maps, and jump quests and awesome NPCs with cool stories. Quest markers and fast travel ruined everything good about open-world games, in my opinion.
  3. I have a stalker. Hi doopers.
  4. I don't want any gameplay that's really complex. I've tried out Elsword, and it's about as complex as I'm interested in. Having game mechanics that are really complicated is fine, as long as the actual gameplay isn't complicated. I want to be able to train while watching some anime, or a stream, or something. But really awesome skill trees, boss fights, quests, puzzles and all that stuff is fine. As long as it's possible to train without paying much attention, even if I do lose some efficiency.
Quitting Maplestory, need a new MMO to play. Recommendations?
I have, and I still play it. :P

I would probably have to say Guild Wars 2 would fit the bill for you.

The bulk of the content is made up of their map Event chains, where something happens and people on the local map either band together to stop the bad event or progress an event forward. It encourages random people to temporarily band together to complete a task, or to get a small gang of buddies together to work on the event for some of the more difficult ones.

Map exploration is rewarded with experience and stuff. Getting 100% map completion is required for the top level gear, and there are neat interactions and random chests and the like littered around for those people who truly want to explore every nook and cranny.

Finally, game play complexities vary between being doable almost AFK and stuff that requires voice coordination between a well-planned party to complete. Most of the stuff you earn for the super hard stuff though is just cosmetic, so you only really have to do that if you really want a particular armor skin.
